# The credit note's refund, linked by `txn_guid:` alone.
#
# The spelling a bank-feed-first ledger uses: the transaction is already in the
# book and the block says which record it settles, leaving the choice of split
# to the run. Both sides being USD, nothing converts and the run takes the
# plain attach.
#
# That is the path a sign guard reaches unconditionally, and reading the
# expected sign from the account's type alone made it refuse this: "a
# settlement of a receivable is negative on it" is true of an invoice and the
# reverse of a credit note, whose posting is −100.00 and whose settlement is
# therefore +100.00. The sign a settlement must have is the opposite of the
# posting's, which is what `_still_owed` has always computed.
#
# What this fixture produces: the +100.00 receivable split in the credit note's
# lot, and the note settled.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "CN-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-06
  credit_note: true
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-06
    description: "Returned goods"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales USD"
    quantity: -1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-06
    due: 2026-02-06
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Credit note CN-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-18
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    txn_guid: "beef0011beef0022beef0033beef0044"
